description.value: This study investigated the efficacy of FDA graphic cigarette warning labels in reducing craving and examined neural and functional connectivity responses in adolescent and adult smokers and non-smokers during fMRI.

spans.text: This study investigates neural responses to the proposed FDA graphic warning labels in adolescent and young adult smokers and non-smokers.

value: We predicted that warning labels showing graphic images vs non-graphic images would elicit reduced craving in smokers, with little effect on non-smokers.

we also hypothesized that smokers would show greater neural activation to the graphic labels in regions implicated in emotion processing [e.g. amygdala ( Due et al. , 2002 ; David et al. , 2005 )], craving [e.g. ventral striatum ( Goldstein and Volkow, 2011 ) and insula ( Naqvi et al. , 2007 )] and craving suppression [e.g. DLPFC ( Kober et al. , 2010 )] and that this effect would be exaggerated in adolescent smokers ( Galván et al. , 2011 , 2013 ).

spans.text: We predicted that warning labels showing graphic images vs non-graphic images would elicit reduced craving in smokers, with little effect on non-smokers.

value: Non-smokers exhibited greater positive functional connectivity between the bilateral amygdala and right DLPFC, right putamen and right nucleus accumbens; between the bilateral insula and DLPFC; and between the bilateral putamen and left DLPFC. Smokers exhibited greater positive functional connectivity than non-smokers between the bilateral insula and right amygdala.

Adolescents exhibited greater positive functional connectivity than adults between the bilateral amygdala and right DLPFC, right nucleus accumbens and right caudate; between the bilateral insula and right DLPFC; and between the bilateral putamen and bilateral DLPFC. Adolescent smokers exhibited greater connectivity than adult smokers between the bilateral amygdala and left parietal lobe, between the bilateral insula and left mPFC and between the bilateral insula and left caudate.

spans.text: A univariate ANOVA revealed a main effect of smoking group, such that non-smokers exhibited greater positive FC between the bilateral amygdala and right DLPFC, right putamen and right nucleus accumbens (NAcc); between the bilateral insula and DLPFC; and between bilateral putamen and left DLPFC. Smokers exhibited greater positive FC than non-smokers between the bilateral insula and right amygdala.
